column3: ping/ping_common.c (4 call sites) -- 3 files, +6/-6","""The rts->rtt counts an exponential weight moving average in a fixed point, that means that even if we limit the triptime to fit into a 32bit number the average will overflow because fixed point needs eight more bits. We also have to limit the triptime to 32bit number because otherwise the moving average may still overflow if we manage to produce a large enough triptime."" Closes the gap on two independent axes: tightens TV_SEC_MAX_VAL from LONG_MAX to INT32_MAX (so a zero-timestamp-derived triptime can no longer be large enough to overflow when squared), and widens rts->rtt from int to uint64_t (so the EWMA accumulator itself cannot overflow even for in-bound triptimes over a long session).","Numerically-correct-but-insufficiently-strict bound

This behavior results in a problem when emulating an instruction with two memory accesses, both of which touch VGA memory... When emulating the 2nd access, the lock that is already being held would be attempted to be re-acquired, resulting in a deadlock.' A SINGLE emulated instruction (e.g. a VGA-to-VGA memory-to-memory move) performing two separate VGA-mapped accesses -- not a nested call within evaluating ONE access -- reaches stdvga_mem_accept() twice before the first access's stdvga_mem_complete() ever runs.","The 2015 fix correctly eliminated the NESTED reentrant-call deadlock (lock acquired, then re-entered from inside the same call's own copy-helper). It did nothing about a structurally different self-deadlock: a SECOND, independent VGA MMIO access performed by the SAME emulated instruction, reached only after the first access's stdvga_mem_accept() call has already returned (still holding the lock) -- both deadlocks share the identical triggering instruction class (rep mov), differing only in which of the instruction's two accesses re-enters the lock.","/* rep mov instruction copying VGA-mapped address A to VGA-mapped address B:
